items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-08-29
items.q: John Russo was the editor at that time.

ctx.x: Well, getting back, I had another question about the Sentinel. You, you talked about, about John Russo. Was, was Russo the editor?

John Russo was the editor at that time. And they had other people in there working under John Russo. I'm trying to think of a young man, well, an old guy, I can't think of his name right now. But he worked there as the assistant editor. He was a very nice man. He's, he's, he's dead now. And, they had a guy by the name of A.C. Jack Moore who contributed sports stories to the Louisiana Weekly. He's going on to his reward also. And, but there was some very nice people in the Informa Sentinel, like I said. It was, it…
Well, when that was, how was, how was the Weekly, the Sentinel, and the Pittsburgh Courier, how was, how were those, how was that competition done?

items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-01-10
items.q: And we elected Johnny Russo, editor of the Courier, Louisiana Dish and President, along with Elgin Hichu of the Louisiana Weekly as vice president.

ctx.x: This is also from the Pittsburgh Courier. This is about that. It's from November 7, 1953 of the Pittsburgh Courier. And so maybe you could read it. It's just a little article.

The Chicago Press and Radio Men and Public Relations representative from several fronts met on that Wednesday in the home of James Okidoki Smith down on St. Anthony Street. And we elected Johnny Russo, editor of the Courier, Louisiana Dish and President, along with Elgin Hichu of the Louisiana Weekly as vice president. Now, Elgin Hichu was born in Houston, Texas, and he died in Houston, Texas. He died of diabetes. And when he left the Louisiana Weekly, he went back to Houston, Texas. And I understand one of his…
I want you to read something. This is something from the Weekly. I think we talked about this.
